subject: LoanBank SOC2: CI artifact signing and secrets escrow evidence

Cc: LoanBank Security Team <corp-audit@loanbank.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CI artifact signing and secrets escrow for SOC2 intake

Hi Mina,

As part of LoanBank's SOC 2 intake we're collecting evidence around build integrity and secrets custody for services that process customer data. Can you provide the following items for Redwood's hosted inference service used by LoanBank?

1) The artifact signing policy and an example signed artifact (hash + signature).
2) Proof of build reproducibility (build command, env snapshot, commit id).
3) CI logs showing the signing step and key access (redacted where appropriate).
4) Key custody mapping: who controls the signing keys, where they are stored (HSM/KMS), and the escrow plan if an admin leaves.
5) The last three key rotation events and associated tickets/approvals.
6) Any automated verification steps you run before deployment (e.g., signature verification on deploy).

Deadline for initial evidence: Thu, Jun 26. If you can point us to a zipped bundle or shared drive link that would be ideal. Also flag anything that is sensitive so we coordinate secure transfer.

Thanks — J.

--
J. Patel
Senior Assessor, AuditLab
j.patel@auditlab.io

Subject: Re: Request: CI artifact signing and secrets escrow for SOC2 intake

Hi J.,

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a focused evidence package that covers each of your bullets. High-level plan below and attachments/links included.

Summary of what we're sharing now (attachments + secure links):
- artifact-signing-policy.pdf — our internal policy describing signing algorithm (RFC4880 GPG v4 compatible), key roles, and rotation cadence (90 days default for ephemeral keys; master signing keys rotated as per change control).
- artifact-verification.zip (Drive/S3 link below) — contains one signed artifact (binary + detached signature), build recipe (Makefile + env snapshot), and a verification script.
- ci-pipeline-snapshot.log — redacted CI job log showing the signing step; key access is via our KMS-bound ephemeral credential broker (described in the matrix).
- secrets-escrow-matrix.csv — mapping of signing key owners, HSM key IDs, escrow custodian (Legal + Security), and recovery playbook reference.

Key notes and controls:
- Signing keys: master key is stored in an HSM (Cloud KMS-backed HSM). Day-to-day signing uses short-lived keys provisioned by an internal signing broker (ephemeral) with auditable STS tokens.
- Escrow: we maintain a dual-escrow model: (1) an encrypted key backup in a customer-specific escrow bucket with 3-of-5 quorum (Legal, Security, and two rotating engineering custodians) and (2) sealed HSM backups accessible only under documented change-control and exec sign-off.
- Reproducible builds: our build agent snapshots include the container image hash, dependency lockfile, and a commit ID. The attached build recipe includes the docker build+tar command and checksums.
- Rotation history: we'll attach a CSV summarizing the last three rotations with ticket IDs (internal Jira links) and approvals.

Secure links (attachments are in the Drive/S3 bundle):
- https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-LoanBank-evidence
- https://s3.redwood-inference.com/audit/loanbank/artifact-verification.zip

Next steps: please confirm if a signed artifact + redacted logs are sufficient for initial review. We can produce HSM audit log extracts if you need deeper evidence (those are more sensitive and require a secure intake channel).

Attaching: artifact-signing-policy.pdf; ci-pipeline-snapshot.log; secrets-escrow-matrix.csv

Regards,

Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 20, 2025 at 11:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Key notes and controls:
> - Signing keys: master key is stored in an HSM (Cloud KMS-backed HSM). Day-to-day signing uses short-lived keys provisioned by an internal signing broker (ephemeral) with auditable STS tokens.

Adding technical detail for the assessor:
- Signing flow (high level):
  1) Developer pushes tag to protected repo branch.
  2) CI triggers a build job running in isolated runner with no persistent credentials.
  3) When binary artifact is produced, CI calls Signing Broker (internal service) with job id and artifact checksum.
  4) Signing Broker requests a one-time signing key from HSM via KMS. The HSM returns a signing handle; the broker performs the signature and the handle is revoked.
  5) Broker writes an immutable audit event to our logging cluster (WORM storage) with key id, signer principal, and signature digest.

- Verification: deployment gates run a verification step: gpg --verify --status-fd 1 artifact.sig artifact.tar.gz which fails the deployment if verification does not match.
- Example key IDs in package: 0xA1B2C3D4E5F60789 (master), 0xF0E1D2C3B4A59687 (ephemeral).
- HSM audit extracts: we can provide a redacted audit log with event timestamps and key handle lifecycles; full audit exports require a secured transfer process.

I'll prepare a short README to sit in the zipped bundle that includes the exact commands and example outputs.

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Mina —

Received, thanks for the quick turnaround and the links. The bundle looks like a good start. A couple of quick asks before we close the intake:

1) Could you include one sample HSM audit log extract (redacted PII) showing a signing handle issuance and revoke event? We only need a 24-hour slice corresponding to the example signed artifact you provided.
2) Please add the Jira ticket IDs in an easily-parsable CSV (if they are links, a short id column is fine).

If you can't share the HSM slice over Drive, let us know and we will provide a secure SFTP endpoint or a short-lived presigned S3 token. Otherwise this is looking in-scope for the SOC2 assessor.

Cheers — J.
